name: Andersonville NHS
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Andersonville National Historic Site in southwestern Georgia preserves the site of Camp Sumter, the largest Confederate military prison during the Civil War. Operational from February 1864 to April 1865, the stockade held up to 32,000 Union prisoners of war in a space originally designed for 10,000, and nearly 13,000 died from disease, malnutrition, and exposure. The site was designated a national historic site in 1970 and also serves as home to the National Prisoner of War Museum, which honors all American prisoners of war throughout the nation's history. The adjacent Andersonville National Cemetery, established in 1865, remains an active national cemetery.
